summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old male with a history of kidney transplantation, atrial fibrillation, diastolic heart failure, and recurrent C. difficile colitis was admitted for acute abdominal pain and shortness of breath. Imaging revealed colitis in the cecum and ascending colon, likely ischemic in origin, along with bilateral pleural effusions and a small pericardial effusion. He was treated for a vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus urinary tract infection and healthcare-associated pneumonia with Augmentin, and recurrent C. difficile was confirmed and managed with oral vancomycin. Acute on chronic heart failure was managed with IV diuresis and re-initiation of torsemide. A colonoscopy showed aphthous ulcers, radiation proctitis, and polyps, with no malignancy. He improved clinically, was weaned off oxygen, and discharged home on a planned antibiotic course, diuretic therapy, and follow-up for polyp removal.
